Originally written from the four-view renders; the per-component evidence is unchanged.
_rule: Anything absent defaults to NOT observable. Marking may only ever weaken the target. See docs/METRIC.md.
_render: view_top, view_bottom, view_top_obl_a, view_top_obl_b, view_bottom_obl_a, view_bottom_obl_b
_values_note: NO component value is printed anywhere on this board. The silkscreen carries reference designators (C1..C10, R1..R14, U1..U3, SW1), header net labels (P00..P46, +5V, 3V3, GND, TX, RX), function labels (POWER, RESET) and the MCU part number STC89C52RC — but no resistances or capacitances. So `value` is false for all 40 components. This is the opposite of case1, where the values were on the silk, and it is why observability is decided per case from the renders.
_terminal_identity_note: Only the through-hole headers get terminal_identity:true, and on two pieces of evidence together: view_bottom shows a SQUARE pad at one end of each header row against round pads elsewhere, which is the pin-1 convention and fixes the numbering; and view_top prints a per-pin silkscreen label along each row, which fixes the order. Everything else is false. U2 is the case that matters most: the LQFP-44 body renders as a plain rounded rectangle with symmetric L-marks at all four corners and NO pin-1 dot, so its 44 pins cannot be numbered from these views. That costs less than it sounds — nearly every U2 pin sits on its own net, so the net structure forces the assignment anyway — but it must not be asserted from the datasheet when the render does not show it.

_refdes_note: 28 of the 40 reference designators are printed on the silkscreen and legible in view_top / view_bottom. Those anchor: the model must read and use them. The twelve that are NOT printed — H1-H5, LED1-LED3, SW2-SW4, USB1 — keep full rename tolerance, and a model may call them anything. Net names are never anchored; the board prints P00 where the netlist says P0.0, and TX/RX for nets called P3.0/P3.1, so requiring the netlist name would mark a correct reading wrong.
